texts.preamble: Iqbal Tea Traders Private Limited vs Calcutta Trading Co on 24 August, 2022 1 In The Court Of Ms.Hemani Malhotra District Judge (Commercial-02)/West Tis Hazari Courts/ Delhi Cnr No:Dlwt010080202018 Cs(Comm)/411/2019 In The Matter Of Iqbal Tea Traders Private Limited A-2 Kirti Nagar, New Delhi-110015 Through its Director Harmanjeet Singh S/o Manjeet Singh ...... Plaintiff Vs. Calcutta Trading Co. 14, Suraj Pole Bazar, Galta Road, Jaipur 302003 Rajasthan ......Defendant Date of Institution : 01.09.2018 Date of final arguments : 22.08.2022 Date of judgment : 24.08.2022 Exparte Judgment
texts.facts: Briefly stated facts of the case are that plaintiff IQBAL TEA TRADERS PRIVATE LIMITED, is a private limited company incorporated under the Indian Companies Act, 1956 and S.Harmanjeet Singh is the Director of the plaintiff company. The plaintiff is carrying on its old established business as merchant and trader of Tea under the name and style of Iqbal Tea Traders Private Limited. The plaintiff's predecessor, Calcutta Tea Co. New Delhi, adopted the mark KESAR for tea on 27.02.1979 and vide assignment deed dated 07.12.2005, the trade mark KESAR registered under No. 506255 dated 01.03.1989 was assigned in favour of the plaintiff company. Thus, the plaintiff company is the legal and lawful owner of registered trade mark KESAR for tea which is registered under Nos. 506255 dated 01.03.1989, 679702 dated 11.09.1995 and 1494121 dated 06.10.2006 in Class 30 and the registration thereof is still valid and subsisting under the Trade Marks Act, 1999. It Iqbal Tea Traders Private Limited vs Calcutta Trading Co on 24 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114190447/ 1 is further the case of plaintiff that due to extensive and exclusive use of the trade mark KESAR by the plaintiff, the same has acquired a distinct identity in relation to the goods for which it is being used by the plaintiff exclusively. The products of the plaintiff under the mark KESAR are of standard quality and public and trade associate the mark KESAR with the products of the plaintiff only. The plaintiff is the proprietor of trade mark KESAR for Tea by virtue of both, i.e. prior adoption, prior use and also registration under the Trade Marks Act, 1999. 2. It is alleged by the plaintiff that no person without the permission or consent of the plaintiff, has any right to use the mark KESAR or any other similar mark which is identical and/or deceptively similar to the registered trade mark KESAR of the plaintiff. The plaintiff has been advertising the mark KESAR by way of advertisements through different medias. The plaintiff is also maintaining a website www.kesartea.com, from which complete business activities of the plaintiff under the mark KESAR can be accessed globally. The annual sales figure of plaintiff's products under the trade mark KESAR have been only increasing since 1991-1992 and in the year 2017-2018, the annual sales figure in rupees was Rs.7, 87, 95, 344.00. 3. In order to protect the mark KESAR for Tea, the plaintiff, from time to time, has filed oppositions against various applications filed by others for registration of mark KESAR or other identical/similar mark b in Class 30 before the Trade Marks Registry Office. 4) On 8th August, 2018 , the plaintiff came to know for the first time that the defendant has launched Tea in market under the mark KESAR and on making investigations and searching the records, it came to notice that the defendant has applied for the registration of mark KESAR under No.1010600 which the plaintiff has already opposed under No. 123810 before the Trade Marks Office and the said application is pending under opposition filed by the plaintiff. Such a misrepresentation is calculated to cause damage and injury to both the plaintiff's business and to its goodwill and reputation. Hence, the present suit. Suit was also accompanied by the application Under Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 r/w Section 151 CPC 5. In the written statement filed by the defendant, claim of plaintiff was denied in toto. It was averred that business of plaintiff was confined within the territory of Delhi whereas the business of defendant was within Jaipur City, hence, there was no question of any confusion in the minds of customers. It was claimed that defendant was sole proprietorship firm of Smt.Geeta Devi Gupta who alongwith her husband was running her business for last 35 years under the name and style of Calcutta Trading Company. It was also claimed that plaintiff was not a manufacturer but a trader like the defendant. It was also averred that the plaintiff was aware of the trade mark of defendant since 2004 and after issuance of notice to defendant, had not taken any action. The defendant had applied for the trade mark in the year 2003-2004, hence, the case of plaintiff was barred by limitation. Iqbal Tea Traders Private Limited vs Calcutta Trading Co on 24 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114190447/ 2 6. Replication was filed by the plaintiff wherein allegations of defendants were denied and averments made in the plaint were reiterated. It was further averred that plaintiff was selling its products not only through traders but also through various online platforms including its own website www.kesartea.com, www.amazon.in and www.indiamart.com . The plaintiff had recently appointed HUSNAL COLLECTIONS, 105/A, Guru Nanak Pura, Jaipur-302004, Rajasthan as its distributor to directly market tea under its mark KESAR in Rajathan. It was also alleged that defendant was selling spurious products under the trade mark of plaintiff on websites www.indiamart.com and www.justdial.in. 7. Vide order dated 23.3.2019 passed by Learned Predecessor of this Court, application under Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 r/w Section 151 CPC filed on behalf of plaintiff, was allowed in favour of plaintiff. Vide the said order, defendant was restrained from carrying on its business and marketing , selling , offering for sale, advertising, distributing or displaying directly or indirectly the products i.e. Tea under trade mark KESAR or under any other identical/deceptively similar trade mark till disposal of the main suit. Subsequent thereto, defendant stopped appearing and it was proceeded exparte vide order dated 11.4.2022 passed by Learned Predecessor of this Court.
texts.arguments: The adoption and use of the impugned identical mark KESAR for Tea on behalf of the defendant is bound to lead to confusion and deception and create an impression that the defendant's products are in some way connected with the products of the plaintiff. 8. In support of it's exparte evidence, plaintiff examined Harmanjeet Singh as PW-1 who filed his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A wherein he reiterated the averments made in the plaint. He also relied on documents viz., Board Resolution as Ex.PW1/1, Assignment Deed as Ex.PW1/2, The Registration Certificates for trade mark Nos.506255,679702 and 1494121 as Ex.PW1/3 to 5, bills/invoices as Ex.PW1/10 to Ex.1/98, newspaper and magazine advertisement of plaintiff's mark Kesar and bills issued by printers, advertising agencies and the letter dated 24.12.2008 of the Govt. of Nct, Prevention of Food Adulteration as Ex.PW1/99 to 163. It was submitted by the Learned. Counsel for the plaintiff that the adoption of a trade mark KESAR identical to plaintiff's trademarks by the defendant is malafide and cannot be a matter of coincidence. The same is a deliberate and a calculated move of the defendant aimed at causing misrepresentation and making illegal profits. The adoption of identical mark/logos by defendant is dishonest and motivated by a desire to usurp the vast reputation and goodwill which is enjoyed by the plaintiff not only in India but throughout the world. It is also submitted that the plaintiff has suffered and is likely to suffer irreparable loss and injury to it's goodwill and reputation on account of aforesaid acts of unfair trade practice committed by the defendant. During the course of arguments, learned counsel for plaintiff brought to the notice of the Court Trade Mark Application number 1010600 of the defendant for registration of trade mark KESAR Tea which was refused on 22.7.2022. Thus, it was claimed that the plaintiff is entitled for the relief(s) claimed in the plaint.
